housing_choice_voucher.description: Provides rental assistance to very low-income families, seniors, and disabled individuals to afford decent, safe housing in the private rental market. Participants pay approximately 30% of their income towards rent, with the program subsidizing the remainder. HUD provides funding and oversight while Marin Housing Authority handles local implementation including eligibility determination, voucher issuance, unit inspections, and landlord payments.
eligible_activities: Tenant-based rental vouchers for private market housing
Mobility counseling to access opportunity neighborhoods

eligibility_requirements.income_limit: Very low income (50% AMI or below)
eligibility_requirements.citizenship: US citizen or eligible immigration status

resident_input_opportunities: Public Housing Authority Plan public hearings
housing_choice_voucher.leverage_point: Residents can participate in Public Housing Authority Plan public hearings and comment periods. Contact the Housing Authority to join resident advisory committees or provide input on program priorities and policies.

contact.address: 4020 Civic Center Drive, San Rafael, CA 94903

special_categories.domestic_violence_victims: Up to 15 placements/year via CalWORKS or Center for Domestic Peace
special_categories.natural_disaster_victims: Up to 15 placements/year via American Red Cross

public_housing.description: Provides affordable rental housing directly owned and managed by Marin Housing Authority, offering safe, subsidized housing to eligible low-income individuals and families. The primary property is Golden Gate Village in Marin City with 296 units. Residents pay no more than 30% of their income for rent.

eligibility_requirements.background_check: No public housing evictions in past 3 years
eligibility_requirements.criminal_history: No felony drug convictions, not a registered sex offender

public_housing.leverage_point: Residents can participate in Golden Gate Village Resident Council and attend public hearings for redevelopment planning. The revitalization project has extensive community input requirements.

below_market_rate_homeownership.description: Offers condominiums and townhomes for sale at below market rate prices to low and moderate-income first-time homebuyers who are priced out of the competitive housing market. MHA administers the program for multiple Marin jurisdictions including County of Marin, San Rafael, Tiburon, San Anselmo, Larkspur, Corte Madera, and Mill Valley.

eligibility_requirements.first_time_buyer: No ownership interest in principal residence in past 3 years
eligibility_requirements.asset_limit: Assets over $100,000 - 10% added to income calculation
eligibility_requirements.citizenship: US citizen or legal permanent resident
eligibility_requirements.education: HUD-approved First Time Homebuyer Workshop certificate required
eligibility_requirements.financing: Must qualify through BMR Participating Lender

below_market_rate_homeownership.leverage_point: Residents can apply through lottery system when units become available. Attend homebuyer workshops to obtain required certificate. Contact MHA for current availability and income limits.
below_market_rate_homeownership.resale_restrictions: Affordability deed restrictions limit future resale profits based on median income increase, CPI, or fair market value (least of three)

hcv_homeownership.description: Allows Housing Choice Voucher (Section 8) recipients to use their Housing Assistance Payment (HAP) subsidy toward mortgage payments instead of rental assistance, enabling transition from renting to homeownership.

eligibility_requirements.voucher_tenure: Must have HCV Rental Voucher for at least 1 year
eligibility_requirements.employment: Head of household employed minimum 1 year at 30 hrs/week (unless elderly/disabled)
eligibility_requirements.savings: Minimum 6% of purchase price for down payment and closing costs (20% realistic)

hcv_homeownership.leverage_point: Current HCV voucher holders can contact MHA to explore homeownership pathway. Assistance lasts maximum 15 years.

cdbg_housing.description: Federal block grant program providing financial assistance to affordable housing developers, nonprofits, and government entities to support housing development and rehabilitation projects aimed at benefiting low and moderate-income persons in Marin County.
eligible_activities: Acquisition of properties for affordable housing

eligibility_requirements.beneficiary_income: Must benefit low and moderate-income persons
eligibility_requirements.fair_housing: Affirmatively Further Fair Housing and submit Affirmative Marketing Plan
eligibility_requirements.green_building: Meet Marin County Green Building Code
eligibility_requirements.accessibility: Comply with UFAS and Title III
eligibility_requirements.section_3: Projects over $200,000 must provide local job opportunities to low-income individuals

resident_input_opportunities: Zoom office hours (1st and 3rd Thursdays, 1-2pm PST)
cdbg_housing.leverage_point: Residents can influence funding priorities through Consolidated Plan public hearings and Annual Action Plan comment periods. Nonprofits can apply during annual NOFA cycle (typically January-February). Community members can attend Zoom office hours for questions.

home_investment_partnerships.description: Federal formula grant program providing funding for affordable housing development, rehabilitation, and rental assistance. Funds support creation of affordable housing for low-income households in Marin County.
eligible_activities: New construction of affordable rental housing
Support for Community Housing Development Organizations (CHDOs)

eligibility_requirements.income_targeting: Must serve households at or below 80% AMI, with emphasis on 50% AMI

home_investment_partnerships.leverage_point: Participate in Consolidated Plan development and Annual Action Plan public comment periods. Housing developers and CHDOs can apply during NOFA cycle.

plha.description: State of California program providing ongoing funding to local governments for affordable housing and homelessness prevention. Funded through Building Homes and Jobs Act recording fees on real estate transactions.

eligibility_requirements.consistency: Projects must be consistent with Housing Element

plha.leverage_point: Participate in Housing Element updates and public hearings. Nonprofits can apply during NOFA cycle for project funding.

marin_affordable_housing_fund.description: County fund providing flexible financing for developers and nonprofits to support development and preservation of affordable housing units throughout Marin County. Applications accepted year-round.

eligibility_requirements.project_type: Must produce or preserve affordable housing units

resident_input_opportunities: Board of Supervisors public hearings on fund allocations
marin_affordable_housing_fund.leverage_point: Developers and nonprofits can apply year-round. Community members can attend Board of Supervisors meetings when funding allocations are discussed.
marin_affordable_housing_fund.application_cycle: Rolling - applications accepted throughout the year

income_limits_2025.note: Income limits published by HUD. Very Low Income for 4-person household is $92,850/year.

marin_housing_authority.address: 4020 Civic Center Drive, San Rafael, CA 94903

marin_county_cda_housing_grants.address: 3501 Civic Center Drive, Suite 308, San Rafael, CA 94903
